title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The policy titled “Decision of the AI Office” outlines the key determinations made by the AI Office regarding the organization’s approach to artificial intelligence. It sets forth the office’s guiding principles, responsibilities, and procedures for overseeing AI development, deployment, and ethical use.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: This policy outlines the creation of new AI office vacancies to hire technology specialists in AI, detailing the roles, responsibilities, and qualifications required for these positions. It also describes the hiring process, reporting structure, and how these specialists will contribute to the organization's AI strategy and projects.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: The document announces a vacancy for the position of Lead Scientific Adviser in the AI Office. It outlines the responsibilities, qualifications, and application process for candidates interested in this leadership role.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: The policy explains how to fill legal officer positions in the AI office, including the qualifications required, the duties expected, and the process for hiring. It emphasizes that these roles are essential for ensuring that AI projects comply with legal standards and ethical guidelines.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: This policy outlines procedures for addressing vacancies in AI Policy Officer roles. It details responsibilities, succession planning, and hiring guidelines to maintain effective AI policy oversight.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts tasked with reviewing the European AI Act and providing scientific and technical guidance to shape its regulations. They assess risks, recommend safeguards, and help balance innovation with safety and accountability in AI systems.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: Draft Standardisation Request is a preliminary document proposing the creation of uniform guidelines for AI practices. It calls for a coordinated effort to define consistent standards that can be adopted across different sectors and jurisdictions.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: This notice announces a consultation for the Community of Practice (CoP), inviting stakeholders to review and comment on upcoming policy or procedural changes. It outlines the consultation period, submission methods, and explains how feedback will shape the CoP’s future direction.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: This document invites people to express interest in joining a Community of Practice (CoP) on a specific topic. It outlines how individuals can submit their interest and what the community aims to achieve.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: The policy explains how the Community of Practice creates and refines its documents through an iterative drafting process. It outlines the steps, collaboration, and revision cycles that help improve the policy over time.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: A graphic that shows the timeline for drafting the policy, mapping out when each part of the drafting process is supposed to happen. It highlights the major milestones, key dates, and overall flow of the drafting work.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: This document presents the initial draft of a Code of Practice, laying out foundational guidelines for the responsible design, use, and oversight of AI systems. It aims to set clear standards for transparency, accountability, and ethical conduct among developers, users, and regulators in the AI industry.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: The document outlines a framework for the responsible use of AI, giving clear guidelines and best practices for developers, users, and regulators. It covers key concerns such as transparency, fairness, accountability, and data protection to help ensure AI systems are safe and trustworthy.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: The Code of Practice: 3rd Draft offers a set of guidelines for the responsible development and deployment of AI systems. It outlines the roles, responsibilities, and best practices that organizations should follow to ensure ethical and compliant AI use.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft outlines a collaborative framework for the responsible development and deployment of artificial intelligence technologies. It proposes shared principles, standards, and commitments designed to ensure AI benefits society while mitigating potential risks.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final is a comprehensive agreement that outlines principles, responsibilities, and safeguards for the responsible development and use of artificial intelligence. It aims to ensure transparency, fairness, and accountability while fostering collaboration among stakeholders to address potential risks and promote societal benefit.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: This document outlines the specific uses of artificial intelligence that are disallowed. It explains the types of AI behaviors and systems that are prohibited, along with the reasons for these restrictions.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: These guidelines explain what a system must do to be considered an AI system, outlining key characteristics such as learning, adaptation, and decision‑support. They help organizations determine which of their technologies need to comply with AI regulations and oversight requirements.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: This policy outlines strategies to improve communication within the startup ecosystem, aiming to boost collaboration and knowledge sharing that fuels innovation. It encourages open dialogue between entrepreneurs, investors, and policymakers to create a supportive environment for emerging businesses.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups aims to give early-stage technology companies access to high‑performance computing resources. It offers funding, training and collaborative opportunities so startups can develop and scale AI and computational solutions.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This policy document outlines the objectives and agenda of a webinar focused on risk management in AI, describing how participants will learn to identify and assess potential AI risks. It also covers strategies for mitigating those risks and ensuring responsible AI deployment.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This webinar covers the fundamentals of risk management, explaining how to identify, assess, and mitigate potential risks in an organization. It also discusses best practices for implementing risk management strategies and the role of AI tools in enhancing decision-making.
